title: Temurah 23
description: Rav Huna and Rabbi Abba give two versions of Rav’s account of the dispute between Rabbi and the Rabbis over a lost sin offering that is found, defend them against the meal-offering baraita, the Yom Kippur goats and the mishna itself, and then Rabbi Ami’s ruling on two piles of money set aside as a guarantee leads to the thirteen horns of the Temple and the midrash of Jehoiada the priest.
topics: 🐐 Rav Huna in Rav’s name: if the owner took one himself, the other dies; the dispute is over one who comes to consult
⚖️ Rabbi Abba in Rav’s name: is an animal designated for a lost one like the lost one?
🥣 Rav Mesharshiyya: the remainder of a meal offering, eaten with non-sacred food so it is eaten while satiated
🎲 The Yom Kippur goats: living animals are not rejected, and a communal sin offering does not die
📏 The tanna teaches a matter that is absolute, not one that depends on other factors
💰 Rabbi Ami: two piles of money as a guarantee, and why Rabbi Shimon needed it
📯 The thirteen horns in the Temple and the six for gift offerings
📜 Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya: the midrash of Jehoiada the priest on the hides of surplus burnt offerings

a1.he: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם מָשַׁךְ אַחַת וְהִקְרִיבָהּ שֶׁהַשְּׁנִיָּה מֵתָה, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לָהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁמָּשַׁךְ אַחַת מֵהֶן וְהִקְרִיב, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל.

a2.he: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּמִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה — שֶׁאֲבוּדָה מֵתָה. עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ? בְּמִתְכַּפֵּר בַּאֲבוּדָה, דְּרַבִּי סָבַר: מַפְרִישׁ לְאִיבּוּד כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: לָאו כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי.

a3.he: רֵישָׁא סְתַם לַן כְּרַבָּנַן, סֵיפָא סְתַם לַן כְּרַבִּי.

a4.he: וּמַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דִּפְלִיגִי רַבִּי וְרַבָּנַן? בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי וְרַבָּנַן בְּסֵיפָא: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וַהֲרֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹמְדוֹת — אַחַת מֵהֶן תִּקְרַב, וּשְׁנִיָּה תָּמוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין חַטָּאת מֵתָה אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת מֵאַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים, וְאֵין מָעוֹת הוֹלְכוֹת לְיָם הַמֶּלַח אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים!

a5.he: הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דָּבָר זֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי וְרַבָּנַן.

a6.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם מָשַׁךְ אַחַת וְהִקְרִיבָהּ — שֶׁהַשְּׁנִיָּה מֵתָה. לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּבָא לִימָּלֵךְ, דְּרַבִּי סָבַר: לֹא עָשׂוּ תַּקָּנָה בְּקָדָשִׁים, וְאָמְרִינַן לָךְ הִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה, וַאֲבוּדָה מֵתָה. וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: עָשׂוּ תַּקָּנָה בַּקֳּדָשִׁים, וְאָמְרִינַן לָךְ הִתְכַּפֵּר בַּאֲבוּדָה, וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה תִּרְעֶה.

a7.he: מוֹתֵיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: וְלֹא עָשׂוּ תַּקָּנָה בַּקֳּדָשִׁים? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״יֹאכְלוּ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה אֲכִילָה מוּעֶטֶת, אוֹכְלִין עִמָּהּ חוּלִּין וּתְרוּמָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא נֶאֱכֶלֶת עַל הַשָּׂבָע.

a8.he: ״יֹאכְלוּהָ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר? שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה אֲכִילָה מְרוּבָּה, אֵין אוֹכְלִין עִמָּהּ חוּלִּין וּתְרוּמָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא נֶאֱכֶלֶת עַל הַגַּסָּה.

a9.he: מַאי לַָאו אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי? לָא, רַבָּנַן.

a10.he: וְרַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּמִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה, שֶׁאֲבוּדָה מֵתָה. עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ? דְּמִתְכַּפֵּר בַּאֲבוּדָה, דְּרַבִּי סָבַר: מַפְרִישׁ לְאִיבּוּד כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: לָאו כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי.

a11.he: תְּנַן: הַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִפְּלוּ דָּמָיו לִנְדָבָה, שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת צִיבּוּר מֵתָה. הָא דְּיָחִיד — מֵתָה.

a12.he: וְאָמַר רַב: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִידְחִין, כְּשֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן מִתְכַּפֵּר, וְאִידַּךְ בָּתְרָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ כְּמַפְרִישׁ לְאִיבּוּד, וְטַעְמָא דְּצִיבּוּר, הָא דְּיָחִיד מֵתָה.

b1.he: מַאי לַָאו אֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן? לָא, רַבִּי הִיא.

b2.he: תְּנַן: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת וְאָבְדָה, וְהִקְרִיב אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ — תָּמוּת.

b3.he: טַעְמָא (דִּקְרֵיבָה) [מִשּׁוּם דְּהִקְרִיבָהּ], הָא לֹא הִקְרִיבָהּ — תִּרְעֶה, לָא שְׁנָא מִתְכַּפֵּר בַּאֲבוּדָה, לָא שְׁנָא מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה, לָא שְׁנָא מָשַׁךְ, וְלָא שְׁנָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ.

b5.he: מִילְּתָא דִּפְסִיקָא לֵיהּ — קָתָנֵי, מִילְּתָא דְּלָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ — לָא קָתָנֵי.

b6.he: תְּנַן: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאת, וְאָבְדוּ, וְהִפְרִישׁ אֲחֵרִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצְאוּ הַמָּעוֹת — יָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b7.he: טַעְמָא דְּמִתְכַּפֵּר מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ, הָא מֵאֶחָד — יוֹלִיכֵם לְיָם הַמֶּלַח.

b8.he: לָא שְׁנָא מִתְכַּפֵּר בַּאֲבוּדָה, וְלָא שְׁנָא מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה, וְלָא שְׁנָא מָשַׁךְ, וְלָא שְׁנָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ — תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ! הָכָא נָמֵי: מִילְּתָא דִּפְסִיקָא לֵיהּ קָתָנֵי, וּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ לָא קָתָנֵי.

b9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הַמַּפְרִישׁ שְׁנֵי צִיבּוּרֵי מָעוֹת לְאַחְרָיוּת, מִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן, וְשֵׁנִי יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b10.he: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי — פְּשִׁיטָא דְּיִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה, עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלָּא בְּמַפְרִישׁ לְאִבּוּד, אֲבָל לְאַחְרָיוּת מוֹדֶה.

b11.he: וְאֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּיִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה, קַל וָחוֹמֶר: הַשְׁתָּא מַפְרִישׁ לְאִיבּוּד אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן לָאו כְּאִיבּוּד דָּמֵי, לְאַחְרָיוּת מִיבַּעְיָא?!

b12.he: וְאֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נְדָבָה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאִית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה.

b13.he: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? וְהָתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר שׁוֹפָרוֹת הָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְהָיָה כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן: ״תִּיקְלִין חַדְתִין״ וְ״עַתִּיקִין״, ״קִינִּין״ וְ״גוֹזְלֵי עוֹלָה״, ״עֵצִים״ וּ״לְבוֹנָה״ וְ״זָהָב לְכַפֹּרֶת״, וְשִׁשָּׁה לִנְדָבָה.

b14.he: וְתָנֵי עֲלַהּ: שִׁשָּׁה לִנְדָבָה — לְעוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת, שֶׁאֵין עוֹרָהּ לַכֹּהֲנִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

b15.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִם כֵּן, בָּטְלָה מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן. דְּתַנְיָא: זֶה מִדְּרַשׁ דָּרַשׁ יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן — ״אָשָׁם הוּא״ כּוּלּוֹ, לְהָבִיא כׇּל דָּבָר הַבָּא מִמּוֹתַר חַטָּאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת, לִיקַּח בְּדָמָיו עוֹלוֹת — הַבָּשָׂר לַשֵּׁם, וְעוֹרוֹת לַכֹּהֲנִים.

b16.he: אַלְמָא אִית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: כִּי אִית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּחַד סִידְרָא,

messages.text: Continued from 22b: the Gemara asked whether the mishna’s first clause can follow the Rabbis while its latter clause follows Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, and noted that this works out well according to Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Gemara

All concede, even the Rabbis, that if the owner did not consult the court about which animal to sacrifice, but instead he took one of the animals and sacrificed it, he has demonstrated a lack of concern for the fate of the remaining animal, and that therefore the second animal is left to die.

notes.he: ואפילו לרבנן דאמרי אבודה בשעת הפרשה רועה מודו שאם משך אחת מהן והקריבה מדעתו דחה האחרת בידים דגלי דעתיה דלא איכפת ליה מינה ואפילו משך האבודה ונתכפר בה והנשארת היא שלא נאבדה מעולם מתה וכי פליגי רבנן היינו בבא לימלך דגלי דעתיה דניחא ליה בתקנתייהו שהפריש חטאת ואבדה והפריש אחרת ונמצאת הראשונה ובא לפנינו לימלך מה יעשה אמרינן ליה לך התכפר באבודה ושאינה אבודה תרעה הא נמי דקתני מאלו ומאלו דמשמע דאם הביא מאחד מהן השני ילך לים המלח ואפילו נתכפר באבודה משכחת לה כגון שמשך מדעתו ולא נמלך דהתם רבנן מודו הלכך תנא הך תקנתא יביא מאלו ומאלו והך תקנתא ניחא ליה טפי מלומר יבוא ויטרח לבית דין וימלך ונאמר לו שיתכפר באבודין ושאינן אבודין יפלו לנדבה:
notes.en: All concede: even according to the Rabbis, who say that [an animal that was] lost at the time of designation grazes, they concede that if he drew one of them and sacrificed it on his own initiative, he has rejected the other with his own hands, for he has revealed his mind that he does not care about it. And even if he drew the lost one and achieved atonement with it, the remaining one, which was never lost, dies. Where the Rabbis disagree is with one who comes to consult, for he has revealed his mind that he wants a remedy for them: he designated a sin offering and it was lost, and he designated another, and the first was found, and he came before us to consult what to do; we say to him: Go achieve atonement with the lost one, and the one that is not lost shall graze. This too, that it teaches “from these and from those,” which implies that if he brought from one of them the second goes to the Dead Sea, even if he achieved atonement with the lost [money]: you find it, for example, where he drew on his own initiative and did not consult, for there the Rabbis concede. Therefore [the tanna] taught this remedy, “he brings from these and from those”; and this remedy suits him better than saying: Let him trouble himself to come to the court and consult, and we will tell him to achieve atonement with the lost [money], and that which is not lost shall go to gift offerings.

notes.dh: (הכל מודים שאם משך אחת מהן והקריבה) רישא רבי וסיפא רבנן
notes.he: ואי קשיא לישני לה נמי לר' אבא מאי הקריב לשחיטה וקודם שחיטה (ראשונה) נמצאת ראשונה תמות ורבי היא דאמר אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה וסיפא ורישא רבי לאו פירכא היא דא"כ אמאי נקט הקריב כלל ליתני הפריש סתמא דבשלמא לרב הונא נקט הקריב לאשמועינן מדעתו דאם משך מדעתו ולא נמלך. לשון רש"י: הכל מודים שאם משך אחת מהן והקריב שהשניה מתה לא נחלקו אלא בבא לימלך וא"ת היכי ניישב לרב הונא לישנא דמתניתין דתנן וחכמים אומרים אין חטאת מתה אלא שנמצאת אחר שכפרו וי"ל דה"ק אין חטאת מתה דלא נוכל למצוא לה תקנה אלא שנמצאת אחר שכפרו דאז אין לה תקנה ולר' אבא נמי נפרש לישנא דמתני' כן:
notes.en: (All concede that if he drew one of them and sacrificed it) The first clause is Rabbi and the latter clause the Rabbis [so the printed heading; the Gemara says the first clause is the Rabbis and the latter Rabbi]: And if it is difficult: let him answer for Rabbi Abba too: What is “sacrificed”? [Brought near] for slaughter, and before the slaughter the first was found, so it dies; and it is Rabbi, who said that one lost at the time of designation dies, and the latter clause and the first clause are both Rabbi. That is no objection, for if so, why did he mention “sacrificed” at all? Let him teach simply “designated.” Granted, according to Rav Huna, he mentioned “sacrificed” to teach us “on his own initiative,” that he drew it on his own and did not consult. Rashi’s wording: “All concede that if he drew one of them and sacrificed it, the second dies; they disagreed only about one who comes to consult.” And if you say: how shall we settle the wording of the mishna according to Rav Huna, where we learned, “And the Rabbis say: A sin offering does not die unless it was found after the owner achieved atonement”? One can say that this is what it is saying: a sin offering does not die such that we cannot find a remedy for it, except where it was found after the owner achieved atonement, for then it has no remedy. And according to Rabbi Abba too we will explain the wording of the mishna this way.

messages.text: Consequently, you find that both clauses of the mishna are consistent with the opinion of the Rabbis, as one may interpret the latter clause as referring to a case where the owner took one of the two sums of money, used it to purchase an animal, and sacrificed the animal, and in such a case, all agree that the other sum of money is cast into the Dead Sea.
But according to that which Rabbi Abba says that Rav says, the mishna cannot be interpreted in this manner. As Rabbi Abba said:

notes.he: אפי' משך מדעתו את האבודה ונתכפר בה אמרי רבנן דתרעה הואיל והיא לא נדחית ולא נאבדה מעולם ואע"ג דלא נמלך ובהא פליגי:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Abba, who said: even if he drew the lost one on his own initiative and achieved atonement with it, the Rabbis say [the other] grazes, since it was neither rejected nor ever lost, even though he did not consult; and it is about this that they disagree.

notes.dh: אלא לר' אבא אמר רב דאמר
notes.he: לקמן נמי הכל מודים [שאם נתכפר בשאין אבודה דאבודה דפיישא מתה על מה נחלקו על נתכפר באבודה ונשתייר' שאינה אבודה]:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Abba, who said that Rav said: below too, “All concede” [that if he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost, the lost one that remains dies; about what did they disagree? About where he achieved atonement with the lost one and the one that is not lost remained].

messages.text: All concede that in a case where one achieves atonement through the one that was not lost, the one that was lost is left to die. With regard to what case do the Rabbis and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi disagree? They disagree with regard to the case of one who achieves atonement with the one that was lost.

As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds that if one designates a sin offering instead of one that was lost, it is considered like the lost sin offering. Accordingly, just as the lost animal is left to die if the second sin offering was sacrificed, the replacement animal is left to die if the original animal was sacrificed.

notes.dh: דרבי סבר מפריש לאבוד כאבוד דמי
notes.he: המפריש תחת קרבן אבוד דינו כאבוד וכי היכי דאם נתכפר בשאינו אבוד מודיתו דמת האבוד הנשאר הכי נמי כי מתכפר באבוד מת שאינו אבוד:
notes.en: For Rabbi holds that one who designates for a lost one, it is like the lost one: one who designates [an animal] in place of a lost offering, its law is like the lost one. Just as, if he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost, you concede that the remaining lost one dies, so too when he achieves atonement with the lost one, the one that is not lost dies.

messages.text: And the Rabbis hold that if one designates a sin offering instead of one that was lost, it is not considered like the lost animal. Rather, if the original animal is sacrificed, the replacement animal is left to graze, as it was never lost.

notes.he: והא דקתני מאלו ומאלו דמשמע הא אם התכפר באחד מהן ואפילו באבודין ילכו שאינן אבודין לים המלח רבי היא ולא רבנן רישא רבנן וסיפא רבי:
notes.en: And the Rabbis hold it is not like the lost one: and that which is taught, “from these and from those,” implying that if he achieved atonement with one of them, even with the lost [money], the [money] that is not lost goes to the Dead Sea, is Rabbi and not the Rabbis. The first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi.

messages.text: Therefore, one must say that according to this explanation, the tanna taught us the first clause of the mishna in an unattributed manner in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and he taught us the latter clause in an unattributed manner in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

notes.he: מה שהפריש תחת האבודה דינו כאבוד מה אבודה כשנשתיירה מתה אף שאינה אבודה אם נשתיירה נמי מתה ורבנן סברי מפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי [אלא אם נשתיירה] שאינה אבודה רועה. וגבי מעות נמי המפריש מעות לחטאתו ואבדה והפריש מעות אחרת תחתיה לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי סברי רבנן ואע"ג דהביא מאלו ולא הביא מאלו הני שאינן אבודין יפלו לנדבה לטעמיה דר' אבא לא מיתוקמא סיפא דדייקינן מינה הא הביא מאלו ולא הביא מאלו [הנך דאישתיירו ילכו לים המלח] כרבנן אלא כר' רישא סתם לן תנא כרבנן וסיפא כר'. אין:
notes.en: For Rabbi holds one who designates for a lost one: what he designated in place of the lost one has the law of the lost one; just as the lost one, when it remains, dies, so too the one that is not lost, if it remains, also dies. And the Rabbis hold one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one, [but if] the one that is not lost [remains], it grazes. And with money too: one who designates money for his sin offering and it was lost, and he designated other money in its stead, the Rabbis hold that [money designated] for a lost one is not like the lost one, and even though he brought from these and did not bring from those, the money that is not lost goes to gift offerings. According to Rabbi Abba’s reasoning, the latter clause, from which we inferred “but if he brought from these and did not bring from those, [what remained goes to the Dead Sea],” cannot be established according to the Rabbis but according to Rabbi: the first clause the tanna taught us unattributed according to the Rabbis, and the latter clause according to Rabbi. Yes.

messages.text: And what is the tanna teaching us by teaching its clauses in accordance with different opinions? Presumably, he is teaching us that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and the Rabbis disagree about this matter. But the tanna already teaches the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and the Rabbis explicitly in the latter clause:

notes.dh: ומאי קמ"ל הני סתמי דפליג ר' ורבנן
notes.he: הא בהדיא קתני לה בסיפא דפליגי המפריש כו':
notes.en: And what does it teach us with these unattributed clauses, that Rabbi and the Rabbis disagree? But it teaches explicitly in the latter clause that they disagree: “One who designates,” etc.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates his sin offering and the animal was lost, and he designated another animal in its stead, and thereafter the first sin offering was found, and both of the animals stand fit for sacrifice, one of them shall be sacrificed and the other shall be left to die; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
A sin offering is not left to die unless it was found after its owner achieved atonement; and the money is not taken to the Dead Sea unless it was found after its owner achieved atonement.

This is what the tanna is teaching us in the latter clause, that this matter that was presented in a contradictory manner between the first and second clauses of the mishna is actually a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and the Rabbis.

notes.dh: הכי קאמר דבר זה מחלוקת רבי ורבנן
notes.he: הך סיפא דקתני לפלוגתא בהדיא הכי קאמר דקא"ל דבר זה הנך בבי דלעיל דפליגי אהדדי חדא רבי וחדא רבנן:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: this matter is a dispute of Rabbi and the Rabbis: the latter clause, which teaches the dispute explicitly, is saying this: it tells us that this matter, those clauses above which conflict with each other, is one Rabbi and one the Rabbis.

notes.he: לשון ירושלמי הניחא לרב הונא דאמר הכל מודים שאם משך אחד מהן והקריב בין נתכפר באבוד בין נתכפר כו' מאי הקריב דקתני רישא והקריב אחרת תחתיה הקריב לשחוט מדעתו - והכי קאמר הקריב אחרת לשחיטה תחתיה וסתם הקריב מדעתו משמע ואחר כך שהקריב אחרת מדעתו לשחיטה נמצאת הראשונה ועדיין לא נשחטה האחרת זו תמות הנותרת ואפילו הניח את זו ונתכפר באבודה הואיל ולא נמלך ורישא וסיפא דברי הכל דהשתא ליכא למידק מרישא הא לא הקריב רועה דהא בדלא הקריב עסקינן וסיפא נמי דקתני יביא מאלו ומאלו אבל אי מייתי מחד מינייהו אזלי אינך לים המלח דברי הכל דמסתמא משמע שהקריב מדעתו בלא נמלך:
notes.en: The Jerusalem version [reads]: “This works out well according to Rav Huna, who said: All concede that if he drew one of them and sacrificed, whether he achieved atonement with the lost one or whether he achieved atonement, etc. What is the ‘sacrificed’ taught in the first clause, ‘and he sacrificed another in its stead’? He brought it near to slaughter on his own initiative.” And this is what it is saying: he brought another near for slaughter in its stead, and an unqualified “brought near” implies on his own initiative; and after he had brought the other near for slaughter on his own, the first was found while the other had not yet been slaughtered: this remaining one dies, even if he set this one aside and achieved atonement with the lost one, since he did not consult. And the first clause and the latter clause are the statement of all, for now one cannot infer from the first clause “but if he did not sacrifice, it grazes,” since we are dealing with a case where he did not [actually] sacrifice. And the latter clause too, which teaches “he brings from these and from those,” but if he brings from one of them the others go to the Dead Sea, is the statement of all, for unqualified, it implies that he sacrificed on his own initiative without consulting.

notes.dh: אלא לר' אבא כו' ורבנן סברי לאו כאבוד דמי
notes.he: ורועה אע"ג דמשך האבודה מדעתו ודחה את זו. השתא ליכא לתרוצי רישא מאי הקריב לשחיטה מדעתו דהא משום משיכה לא מהני מידי אלא ודאי הקריב ממש ואיכא למידק הא לא הקריב רועה השניה וכגון דנתכפר בשאינה אבודה ורבנן היא דמפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי וגבי מעות נמי מפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי וסיפא דמשמע דאי מייתי מחד מינייהו ואפי' שאינן אבודין (חולין) דפיישין אזלי לים המלח לאו כרבנן היא רישא רבנן וסיפא רבי. ואי קשיא לרבי אבא נמי תריץ מאי הקריב לשחיטה וקודם שחיטה נמצאת הראשונה תמות ורבי היא דאמר אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה ורישא וסיפא רבי היא לאו פירכא היא דא"כ אמאי נקט הקריב כלל ליתני הפריש סתמא דבשלמא לרב הונא נקט הקריב לאשמועינן מדעתו דאם משך להקריב ולא נמלך לא עשו לו תקנה:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Abba, etc., and the Rabbis hold it is not like the lost one: and [the other] grazes, even though he drew the lost one on his own initiative and rejected this one. Now one cannot answer the first clause, “What is ‘sacrificed’? Brought near for slaughter on his own,” for on account of drawing nothing is effected; rather, he certainly actually sacrificed, and one may infer: but if he did not sacrifice, the second grazes, where he achieved atonement with the one that was not lost; and it is the Rabbis, [who hold that] one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one. With money too, one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one. And the latter clause, which implies that if he brings from one of them, even the remaining money that is not lost [the printed text has a stray “(Ḥullin)” here] goes to the Dead Sea, is not in accordance with the Rabbis: the first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi. And if it is difficult: for Rabbi Abba too let him answer, “What is ‘sacrificed’? For slaughter, and before the slaughter the first was found, so it dies; and it is Rabbi, who said one lost at the time of designation dies, and the first clause and the latter clause are both Rabbi”: that is no objection, for if so, why did he mention “sacrificed” at all? Let him teach simply “designated.” Granted, according to Rav Huna he mentioned “sacrificed” to teach us “on his own initiative,” that if he drew it to sacrifice and did not consult, they did not make a remedy for him.

notes.he: ל"א הניחא לרב הונא דאמר הכל מודים שאם משך אחת מהן מדעתו כדאמרן והקריב שהשניה דפיישא מתה בין אם נשתיירה אבודה בין אם נשתיירה שאינה אבודה [מתה]:
notes.en: Another version: “This works out well according to Rav Huna, who said: All concede that if he drew one of them on his own initiative,” as we said, “and sacrificed, that the second that remains dies,” whether the lost one remained or the one that is not lost remained, [it dies].

notes.he: דדייקינן ילכו לים המלח אתיא כר' וניחא נמי אליבא דרב הונא דאיכא לאוקומי נמי רישא כר' והיכי דמי דאיכא למימר מאי הקריב (דקתני ברישא) [אחרת תחתיה ואח"כ נמצא הראשנה דקתני לא הפריש ממש קאמר אלא והקריב אחרת תחתיה] לשחיטה מדעתו (ולא הקריב ממש ותמות השניה) [ולא שחטה עד שנמצאת חטאתו האבודה ונתכפר באבודה מדעתו. הראשונה תמות דקתני אההיא ראשונה קאמר דהקריב לשחוטה קודם שנמצאת האבודה להכי קרי ליה ראשונה ותמות משום] דמשך אחת מהן מדעתו ואיכא למימר דאפי' רישא רבי היא וליכא למידק מינה טעמא משום דהקריב דלאו הקריב ממש הוא אלא הקריב לשחיטה. אלא לר' אבא אמר רב דאמר הכל מודים שאם נתכפר כו' לא מיתוקמא סיפא כדדייקינן מינה דילכו לים המלח כלל כרבנן אלא (כר') [לר'] דאמר המפריש לאבוד כאבוד דמי רישא כרבנן וסיפא כר' אין ומאי קמ"ל כו':
notes.en: The latter clause, from which we inferred that [the money] goes to the Dead Sea, accords with Rabbi; and it also works out well according to Rav Huna, for one can establish the first clause too according to Rabbi. How so? One can say: what is “sacrificed” [taught in the first clause, “another in its stead,” and afterward the first was found? It does not mean literally (the bracketed text reads “designated”); rather, he brought another in its stead near] for slaughter on his own initiative [and did not slaughter it until his lost sin offering was found, and he achieved atonement with the lost one on his own. “The first shall die,” which it teaches, refers to that first one, which he brought near to slaughter before the lost one was found; that is why it calls it “first,” and it dies because] he drew one of them on his own initiative. And one can say that even the first clause is Rabbi, and one cannot infer from it that the reason is because he sacrificed, for “sacrificed” does not mean actually sacrificed but brought near for slaughter. But according to Rabbi Abba, who said that Rav said, “All concede that if he achieved atonement,” etc., the latter clause, as we inferred from it that [the money] goes to the Dead Sea, cannot be established according to the Rabbis at all, but according to Rabbi, who said one who designates for a lost one is like the lost one: the first clause is the Rabbis and the latter clause is Rabbi. Yes. And what does it teach us, etc.

messages.text: § The Gemara returns to the matter itself, which was cited above:

All concede that if the owner did not consult the court about which animal to sacrifice but instead took one of the animals and sacrificed it, the second animal is left to die. They disagree only in a case where the owner comes to consult the court.

notes.dh: גופא אמר רב הונא אמר רב הכל מודין שאם משך אחת מהן והקריב מדעתו שהשניה מתה
notes.he: דקנסינן ליה הואיל ועבר מדעתו על מה נחלקו על הבא לימלך איזו יקריב דר' סבר לא עשו תקנה בקדשים דלא איכפת לן בההיא דמתה אלא אמרינן ליה לך התכפר בשאינה אבודה דלא איתיליד ביה ריעותא ואבודה מתה דאיתליד ביה ריעותא ורבנן [סברי עשו תקנה בקדשים כי היכי דלא תמות ואמרינן ליה לך התכפר באבוד כו']:
notes.en: The matter itself: Rav Huna said that Rav said: All concede that if he drew one of them and sacrificed it on his own initiative, the second dies, for we penalize him since he acted on his own. About what did they disagree? About one who comes to consult which one to sacrifice. For Rabbi holds they did not make an ordinance with regard to consecrated items, for we do not care about the one that dies; rather, we say to him: Go achieve atonement with the one that is not lost, in which no defect arose, and the lost one, in which a defect arose, dies. And the Rabbis [hold they made an ordinance with regard to consecrated items, so that it will not die, and we say to him: Go achieve atonement with the lost one, etc.].

messages.text: As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds: The Sages did not care to enact a protective ordinance with regard to consecrated items, and it was of no concern to them that one of the animals would be left to die. And therefore, we say to the owner: Go achieve atonement with the sin offering that was not lost, and the one that was lost shall be left to die.

notes.he: דלא איכפת לן אי מייתא שניה ואמרינן ליה זיל איכפר בשאינה אבודה כו':
notes.en: They did not make an ordinance with regard to consecrated items: we do not care if the second dies, and we say to him: Go achieve atonement with the one that is not lost, etc.

notes.dh: דרבי סבר לא עשו תקנה בקדשים
notes.he: תימה למ"ו הרמ"ר וכי מאבדין קדשים בידים כיון דבידינו לתקן ותירץ כגון שיש ריוח בדבר כגון דאבודה כחושה ושאינה אבודה שמינה דא"ל התכפר בטובה וכחושה תמות:
notes.en: For Rabbi holds they did not make an ordinance with regard to consecrated items: My teacher [abbreviated HaRaMaR] found this astonishing: does one destroy consecrated items with one’s own hands, when it is in our power to remedy it? And he answered: for example, where there is gain in the matter, such as where the lost one is lean and the one that is not lost is fat, for we say to him: Achieve atonement with the good one, and the lean one shall die.

messages.text: And the Rabbis hold: The Sages enacted a protective ordinance with regard to consecrated items, and we therefore say to the owner: Go achieve atonement with the sin offering that was lost, and the one that was not lost shall be left to graze.

notes.he: והכי משמע מתניתין אחת מהן תקרב כדי שתמות השניה שתקרב שאינה אבודה ואבודה תמות דברי רבי וחכמים אומרים אין חטאת מתה כי האי גוונא דבא לימלך דאמרינן ליה התכפר באבודה אלא ההיא דנמצאת לאחר שכיפרו הבעלים ההיא ודאי מתה דליכא תקנתא בהמלכה והוא הדין נמי אם נמצאת קודם ולא נמלך:
notes.en: And the Rabbis hold, etc.: and this is how the mishna is to be understood: “One of them shall be sacrificed and the second shall die,” that the one that is not lost is sacrificed and the lost one dies, “the statement of Rabbi. And the Rabbis say: A sin offering does not die” in a case like this, where he comes to consult, for we say to him: Achieve atonement with the lost one; “but rather” that one which was found after the owner achieved atonement certainly dies, for there is no remedy by consulting; and the same applies if it was found before and he did not consult.

notes.he: והכי נחלקו במתניתין בבא לימלך כר' דאמר דתמות סבירא ליה דאע"ג דבשעת הפרשה אבודה ולא בשעת כפרה אפי' הכי תמות אע"ג דבא לימלך ורבנן סברי אם בא לימלך לעולם אין מתה השניה ולא משכחת לה דמתה אלא ההיא דנמצאת לאחר כפרה (דהא) [דההיא] נתכפר בשאינה אבודה ונשתייר האבודה הלכך מתה (אלא) [אבל] הבא לימלך לעולם לא מתה השניה משום דאמרינן ליה לך התכפר באבודה משום דעשו תקנה בקדשים:
notes.en: And this is how they disagree in the mishna, about one who comes to consult: Rabbi, who said it dies, holds that even though it was lost at the time of designation and not at the time of atonement, even so it dies, even though he comes to consult. And the Rabbis hold that if he comes to consult, the second never dies, and you do not find that it dies except for that which was found after atonement, [for in that case] he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost and the lost one remained; therefore it dies. [But] for one who comes to consult, the second never dies, because we say to him: Go achieve atonement with the lost one, because they made an ordinance with regard to consecrated items.

messages.text: And is there such an opinion that the Sages did not care to enact a protective ordinance with regard to consecrated items, to prevent them from being left to die? But isn’t it taught in a baraita with regard to a verse that deals with the remainder of a meal offering:
messages.quote: The Sages did not care to enact a protective ordinance with regard to consecrated items

messages.text: “And that which is left thereof shall Aaron and his sons eat; it shall be eaten without leaven in a holy place; in the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it” (Leviticus 6:9). Why must the verse state at the end the apparently redundant expression: “They shall eat”? The verse teaches that if the remainder constitutes a small amount for consumption, the priests eat non-sacred food and teruma with it, so that the remainder will be eaten while satiated.

verse.he: וְהַנּוֹתֶרֶת מִמֶּנָּה יֹאכְלוּ אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו מַצּוֹת תֵּאָכֵל בְּמָקוֹם קָדֹשׁ בַּחֲצַר אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד יֹאכְלוּהָ׃
verse.en: What is left of it shall be eaten by Aaron and his sons; it shall be eaten as unleavened cakes, in the sacred precinct; they shall eat it in the enclosure of the Tent of Meeting.

notes.he: גבי שירי מנחה כתיב (ויקרא ו׳:ט׳) והנותרת ממנה יאכלו אהרן ובניו וסיפיה דקרא בחצר אהל מועד יאכלוה וקא דריש יאכלוה קרא יתירא הוא וקאמר יאכלו בלא ה"א יאכלו עמה חולין ותרומה כו'. ואי קשיא הא אין מכניסין חולין לעזרה הא לא קשיא יאכלום מבחוץ ואח"כ יכנסו ויאכלו המנחה כדי שתאכל עם השבע אכילה הוגנת:
notes.en: They shall eat: concerning the remainder of the meal offering it is written (Leviticus 6:9): “And that which is left thereof shall Aaron and his sons eat,” and the end of the verse is “in the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it.” He expounds “they shall eat it” as a superfluous verse, and says: “they shall eat,” without the letter heh: they eat non-sacred food and teruma with it, etc. And if it is difficult: but one does not bring non-sacred food into the Temple courtyard! This is not difficult: they eat them outside, and afterward they enter and eat the meal offering, so that it is eaten while satiated, as a proper eating.

notes.he: ואי קשיא הא אין מכניסין חולין בעזרה הא לא קשיא יאכלוה מבחוץ ואחר כך יכנס ויאכל המנחה לרש"י ועי"ל דאין איסור להכניס חולין בעזרה אלא כשעושה שום עבודה מהן אבל בחנם אין לחוש דהא קמן דאדם נכנס עם בגדים חולין בעזרה:
notes.en: They eat non-sacred food and teruma with it: And if it is difficult: but one does not bring non-sacred food into the Temple courtyard! That is not difficult: they eat it outside and afterward he enters and eats the meal offering, according to Rashi. And one can further say that it is prohibited to bring non-sacred items into the courtyard only when one performs some service with them, but for no purpose there is no concern; for here we see that a person enters the courtyard in non-sacred garments.

messages.text: Furthermore, why must the verse state: “They shall eat it”? The verse teaches that if the remainder constitutes a large amount for consumption, e.g., there are many remainders from the meal offerings, then one does not eat non-sacred food or teruma with it, so that it will not be eaten in an excessive manner. Otherwise, one might fail to consume the entire remainder, and some of it would be rendered leftover from an offering after the time allotted for its consumption [notar].

notes.he: ה"א דיאכלוה קדריש דמשמע יאכלוה לחודה:
notes.en: They shall eat it: he expounds the heh of “they shall eat it” [yokhluha], which implies: they shall eat it alone.

notes.he: שיש להן שירי מנחות הרבה:
notes.en: A large amount for consumption: that they have many remainders of meal offerings.

messages.text: This baraita teaches that an ordinance was enacted in order to prevent the remainder of a meal offering from being rendered notar. The same reasoning should apply to other consecrated items, including a sin offering. What, is it not that this baraita is stated even according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi?

notes.he: וש"מ עשו תקנה בקדשים דקתני לא יאכלו חולין עמה כדי שלא תבוא לידי נותר ותיפסל:
notes.en: What, is it not even Rabbi: and conclude from it that they made an ordinance with regard to consecrated items, for it teaches that they do not eat non-sacred food with it, so that it will not come to be notar and become disqualified.

messages.text: No, this baraita is stated specifically according to the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.he: יאכלו מה ת"ל דכתיב בחצר אהל מועד יאכלוה מה ת"ל דכתיב והנותרת מן המנחה יאכלו אהרן ובניו מצות תאכל במקום קדוש בחצר אהל מועד ולא היה צ"ל יאכלו ולא יאכלוה. אלא יאכלו מה ת"ל שאם היתה מועטת שאם לא היה לו [לכהן] ליכל אלא מעט מן מנחות אוכלין עמה חולין או תרומה כדי שתהא נאכלת מן השבע כדי שיהא באכילתה שביעה וה' דיאכלוה מה ת"ל שאם היתה לו מן המנחות הרבה אין אוכלין [עמה חולין ותרומה כדי שלא תהא המנחה נאכלת מן הגסה לאחר שביעה להכי כתיב יאכלוה היא היא לחודיה] והא הכא אע"ג דכשהיא מרובה אין אוכלין עמה חולין ותרומה כשהיא מועטת עשו תקנה דיאכלו עמה חולין ותרומה אלמא דעשו תקנה בקדשים מאי לאו הא ברייתא אפי' ר' היא דסתמא היא וקשיא לרב הונא דאמר דר' סבר לא עשו תקנה בקדשים לא הא ברייתא רבנן היא:
notes.en: “They shall eat,” what does it teach? [And] “in the court of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it,” what does it teach? For it is written: “And that which is left of the meal offering, Aaron and his sons shall eat; it shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Meeting” [Leviticus 6:9], and it did not need to say “they shall eat” or “they shall eat it.” Rather, “they shall eat,” what does it teach? That if it was a small amount, if [the priest] had only a little of the meal offerings to eat, they eat non-sacred food or teruma with it, so that it is eaten from satiety, so that in eating it there will be satiation. And the heh of “they shall eat it,” what does it teach? That if he had much of the meal offerings, they do not eat [non-sacred food and teruma with it, so that the meal offering is not eaten in excess after satiation; that is why it is written “they shall eat it”: it, by itself]. And here, even though when it is much they do not eat non-sacred food and teruma with it, when it is little they made an ordinance that they eat non-sacred food and teruma with it; evidently they made an ordinance with regard to consecrated items. What, is this baraita not even Rabbi, since it is unattributed? And it is difficult for Rav Huna, who said that Rabbi holds they did not make an ordinance with regard to consecrated items. No, this baraita is the Rabbis.

messages.text: All concede that in a case where one achieves atonement through the one that was not lost, the one that was lost is left to die. With regard to what case do the Rabbis and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi disagree? They disagree with regard to a case where one achieves atonement with the one that was lost.

notes.dh: ור' אבא אמר רב הכל מודים כו'
notes.he: על מה נחלקו על אם נתכפר באבודה דר' סבר כו' והכי פליגי בהכי במתניתין דר' דאמר תמות קסבר אע"ג דאבדה בשעת הפרשה ולא בשעת כפרה ונשתייר שאינה אבודה. אפי' הכי תמות משום דמפריש לאבוד כאבוד דמי אע"ג דשאינה אבודה נשתייר מתה ורבנן סברי אם נשתייר שאינה אבודה אינה מתה דאין חטאת מתה אלא שנמצא לאחר כפרה דהיינו אם נתכפר באבודה ונשתייר שאינה אבודה אין מתה דמפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי:
notes.en: And Rabbi Abba said that Rav said: All concede, etc. About what did they disagree? About where he achieved atonement with the lost one, for Rabbi holds, etc. And this is how they disagree in the mishna: Rabbi, who said it dies, holds that even though it was lost at the time of designation and not at the time of atonement, and the one that is not lost remained, even so it dies, because one who designates for a lost one is like the lost one; even though it is the one that is not lost that remained, it dies. And the Rabbis hold that if the one that is not lost remained, it does not die, for a sin offering dies only if it was found after atonement; that is, if he achieved atonement with the lost one and the one that is not lost remained, it does not die, for one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one.

messages.text: As Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds that if one designates a sin offering instead of one that was lost, it is considered like the lost sin offering. Therefore, the second animal is left to die. And the Rabbis hold that if one designates a sin offering instead of one that was lost, it is not considered like the lost animal. Accordingly, the second animal is left to graze.

messages.caption: Rav Huna and Rabbi Abba: what all concede, and where Rabbi and the Rabbis disagree, in each version of Rav

messages.text: The Gemara objects to the explanation of Rabbi Abba in the name of Rav: We learned in a mishna (Yoma 62a): On Yom Kippur, a pair of goats is brought to the Temple, where lots are drawn to determine which goat is sent to Azazel as the scapegoat, and which goat is sacrificed as a sin offering. If the scapegoat died after the lots were drawn for both goats, another pair of goats is brought and lots are drawn for the second pair. This means that there are two goats that were selected as the sin offering, i.e., the remaining goat from the first pair and the goat selected from the second pair. One of these is sacrificed;
messages.quote: it is not considered like the lost animal

messages.text: and the second goat shall graze until it becomes blemished, and it shall then be sold, and the money received from its sale will be allocated for communal gift offerings. This is because a communal sin offering is not left to die.

notes.he: גבי שעירי יום הכפורים והכי פרישית לה לעיל (תמורה דף כב:):
notes.en: The second shall graze: concerning the goats of Yom Kippur; and I explained it this way above (Temurah 22b).

messages.text: One may infer from the mishna that under similar circumstances, the sin offering of an individual is left to die.

Living animals are not rejected. In other words, the sin offering from the first pair is not disqualified on account of the death of the first scapegoat. And therefore, when he achieves atonement, he may even achieve atonement with the second goat of the first pair.
messages.lead: The Gemara continues its objection: And Rav says with regard to this mishna:

notes.he: במס' יומא (דף סד.):
notes.en: And Rav said: in tractate Yoma (64a).

notes.he: ולא נדחה הראשון במיתת חבירו והוא יקרב ושני שבזוג שני ירעה והאי בתרא הוי ליה כמפריש לאיבוד דמפני הראשון שמת הפרישו שנים האחרים:
notes.en: Living animals are not rejected: the first is not rejected by the death of its fellow, and it is sacrificed, and the second of the second pair grazes. And this latter one is like one who designates for a lost one, for they designated the two others because of the first one that died.

messages.text: And the other sin offering from the latter pair is like an animal designated instead of an offering that was lost, as the second pair was brought due to the death of the first scapegoat. And the mishna states that the reason the remaining sin offering is not left to die is that it is a communal sin offering, but if it were the sin offering of an individual, it would be left to die.

notes.dh: וטעמא דציבור הא דיחיד מתה מאי לאו לרבנן
notes.he: תימה למורי הר"ר אלחנן אמאי לא פריך בהדיא ממתני' דקתני וחכ"א אין חטאת מתה אלא שנמצאת לאחר שכפרו והא הכא דשניהן בעין קודם כפרה וקאמר הא דיחיד מתה ואומר הרר"י דאמתניתין לא מצי למיפרך דאיכא למימר מתניתין הכי קאמר אין חטאת מתה אלא בשנמצאת אחר שכפרו אבל נמצאת קודם כפרה ירעו שניהם עד שיסתאבו וימכרו ויביא מאלו ומאלו חטאת אבל גבי שעירים לא שייך למימר הכי מיהו אפשר דס"ל לרבנן דמתניתין דאם נתכפר באחד מהן אפי' באבודה שניה תמות כי הכא גבי שעירים דלא אפשר לעשות תקנה אחרת דליכא למימר שירעו שניהן ויביא מאלו ומאלו שהרי בו ביום הוא צריך להתכפר באחת מהן ואינו יכול להמתין עבודת היום אבל לרבי אבא דאמר אליבא דרבנן דמפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד ואם נתכפר באבודה שאינה אבודה רועה פריך שפיר דהא הכא דנתכפר בראשון ואפילו הכי דיחיד תמות אלמא מפריש לאבוד כאבוד דמי אבל לרב הונא לא פריך מידי דאיכא למימר דהוי כי משך אחת מהן בלא המלכה בדין שניה למיתה אזלא ביחיד ואפילו לרבנן:
notes.en: And the reason is that it is communal; but an individual’s dies. What, is it not according to the Rabbis: My teacher Rabbi Elḥanan found this astonishing: why does it not object directly from the mishna, which teaches, “And the Rabbis say: A sin offering does not die unless it was found after the owner achieved atonement”? Yet here both are present before atonement, and it says that an individual’s dies! And Rabbi Y. [abbreviated HaRaRY] says that it could not object from the mishna, for one can say that the mishna is saying this: a sin offering does not die except where it was found after the owner achieved atonement; but if it was found before atonement, both graze until they become blemished and are sold, and he brings a sin offering from these and from those. But with the goats it is not relevant to say this. However, it is possible that the Rabbis of the mishna hold that if he achieved atonement with one of them, even the lost one, the second dies, as here with the goats, where it is impossible to make another remedy: one cannot say that both graze and he brings from these and from those, since on that very day he must achieve atonement with one of them and cannot postpone the service of the day. But according to Rabbi Abba, who said according to the Rabbis that one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one, and that if he achieved atonement with the lost one the one that is not lost grazes, it objects well, for here he achieved atonement with the first, and even so an individual’s dies; evidently one who designates for a lost one is like the lost one. But for Rav Huna it poses no objection, for one can say that it is as when he drew one of them without consulting, where by right the second goes to its death in the case of an individual, even according to the Rabbis.

messages.text: What, is it not that this mishna is stated even in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis? If so, the mishna is teaching that even according to the Rabbis, an offering designated in the stead of a lost animal is considered like the lost animal, which would contradict the statement of Rabbi Abba.

notes.he: וש"מ כאבודה דמי דנתכפר בראשון חבירו של אבוד וזה שלא נאבד לא הוא ולא חבירו אזלי למיתה אי הוו דיחיד אלמא טעמייהו דרבנן לאו משום הכי הוא:
notes.en: What, is it not the Rabbis: and conclude from it that it is like the lost one; for he achieved atonement with the first, the fellow of the lost one, and this one, of which neither it nor its fellow was lost, would go to its death if they were an individual’s. Evidently the Rabbis’ reason is not this.

messages.text: No, it is stated only in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

notes.dh: ואמר רב דפליג עליה דר' יוחנן
notes.he: בעלי חיין שאין בהן פסול אינן נדחין וכשהוא מתכפר בשני שבזוג ראשון מתכפר משום דבעלי חיין אינן נדחין ואידך בתרא שני שבזוג שני הוה ליה כמפריש לאבוד תחת ההוא דמת דהיינו אבוד וקתני ירעה טעמא דחטאת דציבור הוא הא דיחיד מתה מאי לאו אפי' הא מתניתין רבנן היא וקשיא לר' אבא דאמר דלרבנן מפריש לאבוד לאו כאבוד דמי ורועה לא ההיא מתניתין ר' היא ולא רבנן. שני צבורי מעות לאחריות שאם יאבד צבור אחד שיתכפרו באחד]:
notes.en: And Rav said, disagreeing with Rabbi Yoḥanan: living animals in which there is no disqualification are not rejected, and when he achieves atonement, he achieves atonement with the second of the first pair, because living animals are not rejected; and the other, the latter one, the second of the second pair, is like one designated for a lost one, in place of the one that died, which is the lost one; and it teaches “it grazes.” The reason is that it is a communal sin offering; but an individual’s dies. What, is this mishna not even the Rabbis? And it is difficult for Rabbi Abba, who said that according to the Rabbis one who designates for a lost one is not like the lost one, and it grazes. No, that mishna is Rabbi and not the Rabbis. [His next words, on Rabbi Ami below:] Two piles of money as a guarantee: so that if one pile is lost they will achieve atonement with one.

messages.text: The Gemara poses a challenge to the explanations of both Rav Huna and Rabbi Abba from that which we learned in the mishna:

In the case of one who designates a sin offering, and the animal was lost, and he designated another in its stead and sacrificed it, and the first animal was subsequently found, that is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal, and it shall be left to die.

The reason that the original animal is left to die is that the second animal was already sacrificed, but if the owner did not sacrifice the second animal before the original animal was found, then the original animal is left to graze.
messages.quote: he designated another in its stead and sacrificed it

notes.dh: הא נמצא מעיקרא קודם כפרה רועה לא שנא מתכפר כו'
notes.he: וקשיא לתרוייהו בין לרב הונא בין לר' אבא:
notes.en: But if it was found at the outset, before atonement, it grazes, no difference whether he achieves atonement, etc. And it is difficult for both of them, both for Rav Huna and for Rabbi Abba.

messages.text: The mishna apparently indicates that there is no difference whether he achieves atonement with the sin offering that was lost and there is no difference whether he achieves atonement with the sin offering that was not lost. It can likewise be inferred from the mishna that there is no difference whether he took the animal and sacrificed it without consulting the court and there is no difference whether he did not take the animal and sacrifice it without consulting the court. In all cases, if the owner had not yet achieved atonement then the remaining animal is left to graze.

If so, this is a conclusive refutation of the opinions of both of them, since according to Rav Huna everyone agrees that an animal is left to die if the owner took one of the animals without consulting the court; and according to Rabbi Abba everyone agrees that if the owner achieved atonement with the second animal, the lost animal is left to die.

notes.he: דרב הונא ודרבי אבא:
notes.en: Of both of them: of Rav Huna and of Rabbi Abba.

messages.text: One should not infer in that manner from the mishna. Rather, the tanna of the mishna taught a matter that was absolute, i.e., a case where the second animal was sacrificed before the original animal was found, as the lost animal is always left to die.

notes.he:
כלומר לא תימא הא לא הקריב רועה דזימנין דרועה וזימנין דמתה כגון לרב הונא משך ושוב הקריב אפילו האבודה שאינה אבודה מתה בא לימלך רועה ולרבי אבא בין משך בין נמלך אם נתכפר בשאינה אבודה אבודה מתה ואם באבודה נתכפר זו רועה והאי דקתני הקריב קודם מציאת הראשונה משום דהא פסיקא ליה דמתה ואין חילוק בדבר ומשום הכי לא תנא נמצאת קודם כפרה מתה ולוקמא לרב הונא בדלא נמלך ולרבי אבא בנתכפר בשאינה אבודה משום דהיכא דנמצאת קודם כפרה מילתא דלא פסיקא היא דבעי לשוויי חילוק אי זו רועה ואי זו מתה.
ל"א הא נמצאת מעיקרא תרעה הניחא דקריב האבודה כו' והיינו הך אלא שלשון ירושלמי הוא:
notes.en: It teaches a matter that is absolute for it: that is to say, do not say “but if he did not sacrifice, it grazes,” for sometimes it grazes and sometimes it dies. For example, according to Rav Huna: if he drew and then sacrificed, even the lost one, the one that is not lost dies; if he came to consult, it grazes. And according to Rabbi Abba: whether he drew or consulted, if he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost, the lost one dies, and if he achieved atonement with the lost one, this one grazes. And the reason it teaches “sacrificed” before the first was found is that this is absolute for it, that it dies, with no distinction in the matter. And for this reason it did not teach “found before atonement, it dies,” establishing it, according to Rav Huna, where he did not consult, and according to Rabbi Abba, where he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost: because where it was found before atonement it is a matter that is not absolute, for it would need to set out a distinction as to which one grazes and which one dies. Another version: “But if it was found at the outset, it grazes: this works out well where he sacrificed the lost one,” etc.; and it is the same thing, except that it is the Jerusalem version.

notes.dh: לא הא לא קשיא להו דמילתא דפשיטא ליה לתנא קתני
notes.he: היינו המפריש חטאתו ואבדה [ואח"כ נמצאת הראשונה] לאחר כפרה דתמות היינו פשיטא ליה ותני תמות. אבל הא דוקיא הא נמצא מעיקרא לא קתני דלא פשיטא ליה דפעמים רועה ופעמים מתה לר' הונא כדאית ליה דכי משך אחת מדעתו השניה מתה ולא רועה. ולרבי אבא כדאית ליה דאם נתכפר בשאינה אבודה שאבודה מתה אע"ג דנאבדה בשעת הפרשת שניה ולא בשעת כפרה אפי' הכי מתה ולא רועה הואיל ולא פשיטא ליה למתני רועה לעולם ולא קתני הלכך לא קשיא:
notes.en: No, this is not difficult for them, for the tanna teaches a matter that is obvious to him. That is: one who designates his sin offering and it was lost, [and afterward the first was found] after atonement, it dies; this is obvious to him, and he teaches “it dies.” But this inference, “but if it was found at the outset,” he does not teach, because it is not obvious to him, for sometimes it grazes and sometimes it dies: for Rav Huna according to his view, that when he drew one on his own initiative the second dies and does not graze; and for Rabbi Abba according to his view, that if he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost, the lost one dies, even though it was lost at the time the second was designated and not at the time of atonement, even so it dies and does not graze. Since it is not obvious to him to teach “it grazes” always, he does not teach it; therefore it is not difficult.

messages.text: He did not teach a matter that was not absolute, i.e., a matter that depends on some other factor, e.g., whether the owner took the animal without consulting the court, or whether the owner achieved atonement with the lost animal.

notes.he: כלומר ניתני נמצא מעיקרא ואחר כך תמות ונוקמה לדרב הונא בנמשך ולר' אבא בנתכפר בשאינה אבודה:
notes.en: And let it teach “found at the outset”: that is to say, let it teach “found at the outset” and afterward “it dies,” and establish it, for Rav Huna, where he drew it, and for Rabbi Abba, where he achieved atonement with the one that is not lost.

notes.he: ומשני מילתא דפסיקא ליה קתני כו':
notes.en: And it answers: It teaches a matter that is absolute for it, etc.

notes.he: ל"א הא נמצא מעיקרא רועה הניחא לר' אבא קא מתרץ האי לישנא הניחא דדייקת הא נמצא מעיקרא רועה הני מילי היכא דהקריב אבודה ונשתיירה שאינה אבודה אלא אם הקריב שאינה אבודה ונשתיירה אבודה אמאי רועה מתה איבעי ליה למיתנא:
notes.en: Another version: “But if it was found at the outset, it grazes; this works out well…”: this version answers for Rabbi Abba. It works out well that you inferred “but if it was found at the outset, it grazes” where he sacrificed the lost one and the one that is not lost remained. But if he sacrificed the one that is not lost and the lost one remained, why does it graze? It dies, and it should have taught that.

notes.he: כי דייקינן הא נמצא מעיקרא רועה כגון דהקריב אבודה ונשתיירה שאינה אבודה משום הכי רועה:
notes.en: Rabbi Abba holds: when we infer “but if it was found at the outset, it grazes,” it is, for example, where he sacrificed the lost one and the one that is not lost remained; that is why it grazes.

notes.he: דבההיא עסקינן:
notes.en: If so: that we are dealing with that case.

notes.he: הקריב ואח"כ נמצא מתה נתני נמצאה מעיקרא והקריב כו'. וכ"ש הקריב ואח"כ נמצא דמתה:
notes.en: Why does the mishna specifically teach [“he sacrificed and afterward it was found, it dies”]? Let it teach “it was found at the outset and he sacrificed,” etc., and all the more so “he sacrificed and afterward it was found,” that it dies.

notes.he: דודאי מתה [לא קתני] דהא פעמים מתה פעמים רועה דאם נתכפר באבודה ונשתיירה שאינה אבודה רועה הלכך לא תני לה מתניתין אבל הקריב ואח"כ נמצא דפסיקא ליה דודאי מתה תני לה:
notes.en: That which is not absolute for it, [that it] certainly dies, [it does not teach], for sometimes it dies and sometimes it grazes: if he achieved atonement with the lost one and the one that is not lost remained, it grazes; therefore the mishna does not teach it. But “he sacrificed and afterward it was found,” which is absolute for it, that it certainly dies, it teaches.

messages.text: The Gemara poses another difficulty from that which we learned in the mishna:

notes.he: (כפירוש דלישנא קמא) [בהילוכא דתנן המפריש חטאתו] דלעיל ובלישנא אחרת מותיב לר' אבא לחוד:
notes.en: We learned: One who designates money for his sin offering, etc.: [along the same course as we learned above, “one who designates his sin offering”]; and in another version it objects to Rabbi Abba alone.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost, and he designated other money in its stead, and thereafter the original money was found, he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

The reason that the remainder is allocated for communal gift offerings is that he atones by bringing a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead, but if the owner brought a sin offering from one of the two sums of money, he must take the other money and cast it into the Dead Sea.
messages.quote: he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead

notes.he: מינייהו יוליך השני לים המלח כו'. וקס"ד דדברי הכל היא אלמא טעמייהו דרבנן לאו בהכי הוא:
notes.en: But [if he brought] from one: of them, he takes the second to the Dead Sea, etc. And it enters [the questioner’s] mind that it is the statement of all; evidently the Rabbis’ reason is not this.

notes.dh: הא מאחד מהן יוליכם לים המלח כו'
notes.he: תיובתא דתרוייהו תימה דלעיל פריך מינה וקאמר הניחא לרב הונא ולרבי אבא נמי משני לה כרבי והכא פריך מינה לתרוייהו וצ"ל דלית ליה השתא כסוגיא דלעיל אלא מסתברא ליה למקשה דהכא דאתיא נמי כרבנן ומיירי בכל ענין וכן דרך הש"ס להפך קושייתו בכל ענין פעמים ככה ופעמים ככה:
notes.en: But [if he brought] from one of them he takes them to the Dead Sea, etc., a refutation of both of them: It is astonishing: above it objected from this and said, “This works out well according to Rav Huna,” and for Rabbi Abba too it answered it according to Rabbi; and here it objects from it against both of them! One must say that [the questioner] now does not hold like the passage above; rather, it seems reasonable to the questioner here that it accords with the Rabbis as well and speaks of every case. And such is the way of the Talmud, to turn its question in every direction, sometimes this way and sometimes that.

notes.he: קסבר ר' אבא כי קתני דילכו לים המלח בשהביא משאין אבודין דאבודין נשתיירו:
notes.en: Rabbi Abba holds: when it teaches that they go to the Dead Sea, it is where he brought from the money that is not lost and the lost money remained.

messages.text: The mishna apparently indicates that there is no difference whether he achieves atonement with the money that was lost and there is no difference whether he achieves atonement with the money that was not lost, and there is no difference whether he took the money and brought a sin offering without consulting the court and there is no difference whether he did not take the money without consulting the court. In all cases, the other money is cast into the Dead Sea. If so, this is a conclusive refutation of the opinions of both Rav Huna and Rabbi Abba, as the mishna does not conform to either explanation.
Here too, the tanna taught a matter that was absolute, i.e., a case where the owner achieved atonement with one of the two sums of money, but he did not teach a matter that was not absolute.

notes.dh: הכא נמי מילתא דפסיקא ליה כו'
notes.he: כלומר לא תימא הא מחד מינייהו ילכו לים המלח דזימנין אזלי לים המלח וזימנין לנדבה למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה והאי דתנא מאלו ולא תנא יביא מאחד מהן משום דמילתא דפסיקא ליה קתני דהאי ודאי תקנתא גמורה היא בלא שום חילוק אבל אי תנא יביא מאחד מהן בעי לחלוקי בין משך ללא משך לרב הונא ולרבי אבא בין אבודין לשאינן אבודין:
notes.en: Here too, it teaches a matter that is absolute for it, etc.: that is to say, do not say “but [if he brought] from one of them, they go to the Dead Sea,” for sometimes they go to the Dead Sea and sometimes to gift offerings, for each Sage according to his view. And the reason it taught “from these and from those” and did not teach “he brings from one of them” is that it teaches a matter that is absolute for it, for this is certainly a complete remedy without any distinction; but had it taught “he brings from one of them,” it would have needed to distinguish, for Rav Huna, between drawing and not drawing, and for Rabbi Abba, between the lost money and that which is not lost.

notes.dh: אי הכי מאי אריא תני כו'
notes.he: בהילוכא דלעיל [ת"ש השני בשני שעירי יוה"כ קא מיירי היכא דמת אחד מהן משהגריל והביא שנים והגריל עליהן כדאמרן לעיל השני ירעה כו':
notes.en: If so, why does it specifically teach, etc.: along the course above. [Come and hear: “The second”: this speaks of the two goats of Yom Kippur, where one of them died after he drew the lots, and he brought two and drew lots over them, as we said above: “The second shall graze,” etc.]

messages.text: In the case of one who designates two piles of money as a guarantee, so that in the event that one pile is lost he will purchase his sin offering with the other pile, he achieves atonement with one of them, and the second pile is allocated for communal gift offerings.
messages.lead: § With regard to designating money for purchasing a sin offering:

notes.he: שאם יאבד אחד מהן יתכפר בחבירו:
notes.en: As a guarantee: that if one of them is lost he will achieve atonement with its fellow.

notes.dh: המפריש שני ציבורי מעות לאחריות כו'
notes.he: אי אליבא דרבי פשיטא ולקמן גבי מפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות מוקי לה כרבי ולא פריך פשיטא דיש לחלק בין מפריש מעות לאחריות למפריש בהמות לאחריות דהא קמן לרבי שמעון נמי דאמר גבי בהמות דמתה גבי ציבורי מעות מודה דמתכפר באחת מהן והשני רועה:
notes.en: One who designates two piles of money as a guarantee, etc.: If according to Rabbi, it is obvious. And below, regarding one who designates two sin offerings as a guarantee, it establishes it according to Rabbi and does not object “it is obvious.” For one can distinguish between one who designates money as a guarantee and one who designates animals as a guarantee; for here we see that even Rabbi Shimon, who says with regard to animals that it dies, concedes with regard to piles of money that he achieves atonement with one of them and the second “grazes” [i.e., is not destroyed].

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this statement? If we say that it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, it is obvious that the second pile of money is allocated for communal gift offerings, as Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says that the surplus money is cast into the Dead Sea only in a case where one designated the money instead of money that was lost. But if one separated the two sums of money at the same time as a guarantee, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi concedes that the unused money is allocated for gift offerings.
messages.quote: the second pile is allocated for communal gift offerings

notes.he: ל"א פשיטא דלרבנן יפלו לנדבה דהשתא יש לומר כו' ואלא לר' אליבא דר' פשיטא ע"כ לא קאמר ר' דמתה אלא במפריש לאבוד אבל באחריות מודה דיפלו לנדבה [דהא ליכא אבוד]:
notes.en: Another version: “It is obvious that according to the Rabbis they go to gift offerings, for now one can say,” etc. And rather according to Rabbi: according to Rabbi it is obvious, for Rabbi said that it dies only in one who designates for a lost one, but with a guarantee he concedes that they go to gift offerings [for there is no lost one].

messages.text: Rather, you will say that it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis. But if so, isn’t it obvious that the unused money is allocated for communal gift offerings, due to the following a fortiori inference: Now that the Rabbis say with regard to one who designates money to replace money that was lost that it is not considered like the lost money and is not cast into the Dead Sea, is it necessary to teach that money designated as a guarantee is allocated for communal gift offerings and is not cast into the sea?

notes.he: דשני יפלו לנדבה:
notes.en: Is it necessary [to say this] as a guarantee: that the second goes to gift offerings?

messages.text: Rather, it was necessary for Rabbi Ami to teach this halakha according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who holds that whenever the owner achieved atonement with another sin offering the remaining animal is left to die, even if it was initially designated as a guarantee.

notes.he: דאמר באידך פירקין דלעיל (תמורה דף טו.) חמש חטאות מתות ולית ליה רועה לגמרי שיפלו דמים לנדבה:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Shimon: who said in the other chapter above (Temurah 15a) that five sin offerings die, and he does not hold of “grazes” at all, such that the money would go to gift offerings.

messages.text: Lest you say that just as Rabbi Shimon does not hold that an animal is left to graze if the owner achieved atonement with another animal, he also does not maintain that the unused money is allocated for communal gift offerings, Rabbi Ami teaches us that even Rabbi Shimon holds that if one separates additional money as a guarantee, the unused money is allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.dh: מהו דתימא לית ליה לר"ש נדבה
notes.he: גבי חטאת דכי היכי דלית ליה גבי בהמות לית ליה נמי גבי מעות קא משמע לן:
notes.en: Lest you say Rabbi Shimon does not hold of gift offerings: with regard to a sin offering, that just as he does not hold of it with animals, he also does not hold of it with money; it teaches us [that he does].

notes.dh: אלא אליבא דר' שמעון איצטריכא ליה
notes.he: דאמר כל חמש חטאות מיתות (אפילו) [חדא] חטאת שכפרו בעליה דמהו דתימא ההיא צבור שני דנשתייר ליהוי כמותר חטאת שכפרו בעליה ולימות ולא ליפלו לנדבה דלר' שמעון נדבה במותר חטאת לית ליה קמ"ל ר' אמי דאית ליה:
notes.en: Rather, it was necessary according to Rabbi Shimon, who said all five sin offerings die, [one of them] a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement. Lest you say that the second pile which remained should be like the surplus of a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement, and should die and not go to gift offerings, for Rabbi Shimon does not hold of gift offerings from the surplus of a sin offering, Rabbi Ami teaches us that he does hold of it.

messages.text: But how can you say that one might think that Rabbi Shimon does not hold that the unused money is allocated for communal gift offerings? Isn’t it taught in a mishna (Shekalim 18a):

notes.dh: ומי מצית אמרת דלית ליה נדבה
notes.he: במותר חטאת:
notes.en: And can you say that he does not hold of gift offerings: from the surplus of a sin offering?

messages.text: There were thirteen collection horns in the Temple, and the intended use of the funds was written upon each one, as follows: New shekels, for shekels given for the current year; and old shekels, for shekels given belatedly for the previous year; pairs of birds, whose funds were used to purchase obligatory bird offerings, e.g., for a woman who gave birth; and fledglings designated for voluntary burnt offerings; wood for the arrangement on the altar; and frankincense that accompanied meal offerings; and gold donated for the Ark Cover.

notes.he: מי שלא הביא שקלו באדר מביאו כל השנה ונותנו באותו שופר וכשיגיע אחד מן השלשה פרקים שתורמין את הלשכה נותנן בלשכה ונתרם עם שאר כסף שבלשכה:
notes.en: New shekels [tiklin ḥadtin]: one who did not bring his shekel in Adar brings it all year and puts it in that horn; and when one of the three times arrives at which they take up [funds] from the chamber, they put them in the chamber, and it is taken up with the rest of the silver in the chamber.

notes.he: מי שלא הביא שקלו אשתקד מביאו לשנה הבאה ונותנו שם והן עושין מהן חומת העיר ומגדלותיה וכל צרכי העיר שהרי ממותר שירי הלשכה לבד נעשה כאותה ששנינו (שקלים פ"ד מ"ב) מותר שירי הלשכה ממנה היו עושין חומות העיר כו' והאי מותר הוא שאילו היה שם היה נשאר:
notes.en: And on the second was written “old”: one who did not bring his shekel last year brings it the following year and puts it there, and from them they make the city wall and its towers and all the needs of the city; for [these] were made only from the surplus of the remainder in the chamber, as we learned (Shekalim 4:2): “The surplus of the remainder in the chamber: from it they would make the walls of the city,” etc. And this is surplus, for had it been there [in its year], it would have been left over.

notes.he: מי שהיה מחוסר כפרה כגון זב וזבה ויולדת ומצורע שהן מביאין קן מביא מעות ונותן שם ואוכל בקדשים לערב בחזקת שהוקרבה כפרתו שאין בית דין של כהנים עומדין משם עד שיכלו כל המעות שבאותו שופר כדי שלא יאכל מחוסר כפרה בקדשים:
notes.en: Pairs [kinin]: one who was lacking atonement, such as a zav, a zava, a woman after childbirth and a leper, who bring a pair of birds, brings money and puts it there, and eats consecrated food in the evening on the presumption that his atonement offering has been sacrificed; for the court of priests does not leave there until all the money in that horn is used up, so that one lacking atonement will not eat consecrated food.

notes.he: ברביעי כתוב כן והמתנדב בני יונה לנדבת עולת העוף מביא מעות ונותן בו:
notes.en: Fledglings for burnt offerings: on the fourth this was written; and one who donates young doves as a voluntary bird burnt offering brings money and puts it in.

notes.he: בחמישית כתוב עצים שהמתנדב עצים למערכה מביא מעות ונותן לתוכו:
notes.en: Wood: on the fifth was written “wood,” for one who donates wood for the arrangement [on the altar] brings money and puts it in.

notes.he: בששי כתוב לבונה שהמתנדב לבונה מטיל מעות לתוכו:
notes.en: Frankincense: on the sixth was written “frankincense,” for one who donates frankincense casts money into it.

notes.he: המתנדב לכלי שרת מביא ונותן בו. ל"א וזהב לכפורת המתנדב כלי שרת מביא ונותן. כפורת היינו מזרק ובספר עזרא כתיב כפורי זהב וגו' ומש"ה נראה לי שהוא עיקר משום דקדשי בדק הבית לא היו באין למקדש אלא ליד הגזבר:
notes.en: And gold for the Ark Cover [kapporet]: one who donates for service vessels brings [money] and puts it in. Another version: “And gold for the kapporet”: one who donates service vessels brings and puts it in; kapporet means a basin, and in the book of Ezra it is written “golden bowls [kefori zahav],” etc. And for this reason it seems to me that this is the main [explanation], because things consecrated for Temple maintenance did not come to the Temple but to the hand of the treasurer.

notes.dh: [והתנן י"ג שופרות היו במקדש [והיה כתוב] עליהן תיקלין חדתין
notes.he: אינהו הוו לקרבנות של כל השנה תיקלין עתיקין שמי שלא שקל אישתקד ישקול עכשיו ויניח באותו שופר]:
notes.en: [But didn’t we learn: There were thirteen horns in the Temple, (and it was written) on them: “New shekels”: these were for the offerings of the whole year. “Old shekels”: one who did not give his shekel last year gives it now and puts it in that horn.]

notes.he: הן תורין:
notes.en: Pairs [kinin]: these are turtledoves.

notes.he: הן בני יונה:
notes.en: And fledglings for burnt offerings: these are young doves.

notes.he: שמאותן מעות שבאותו שופר קונין עצים לצורך המערכה:
notes.en: Wood: with the money in that horn they buy wood for the needs of the arrangement [on the altar].

notes.he: לצורך קניית לבונה:
notes.en: And frankincense: for the purchase of frankincense.

notes.he: שמהן זהב לצורך כפורת ואיכא דאמרי זהב לכפורת לצורך בדק הבית לכלים המצופים זהב. לשון מורי הגאון:
notes.en: And gold: from which [comes] gold for the needs of the kapporet. And some say: gold for the kapporet, for the needs of Temple maintenance, for vessels overlaid with gold. The wording of my teacher, the Gaon.

messages.text: And the remaining six horns were designated for the purchase of communal gift offerings.

notes.dh: וששה שופרות היו לנדבת צבור הבאה מן המותרות
notes.he: דחטאות ואשמות וכל הנך דאמרינן יפלו דמיו לנדבה. ובפרק בתרא דמנחות (דף קז:) מפרש הני ששה כנגד מי:
notes.en: And six horns were for communal gift offerings that come from surplus: of sin offerings and guilt offerings, and all those of which we say “its money shall be allocated for gift offerings.” And in the last chapter of Menaḥot (107b) it explains what these six correspond to.

notes.he: בפרק בתרא דמנחות (דף קז:) פליגי בה אמוראי הני ששה כנגד מי חזקיה אמר כנגד ששה בתי אבות שיהיה להם שלום זה כנגד זה לפיכך תיקנו ששה כנגד ו' ימי החול שיהא לכל בית אב ליומו וזעירי אמר כנגד פר ועגל וכבש איל גדי ושעיר וכל כך למה (כדי) שלא היו רוצין לעשות ממותר דמי הפר אלא לפר בלבד וכן לכל אחד ואע"ג דאיכא [מ"ד] בפ"ק דשבועות (דף יב:) מקיצים בעולת העוף הני מילי דיעבד אבל לכתחילה לא דטוב לעשות מהן למה שהופרשו תחילה:
notes.en: And six for gift offerings: In the last chapter of Menaḥot (107b) Amoraim disagree about what these six correspond to. Ḥizkiyya said: to the six priestly families [battei avot], so that they would be at peace with one another; therefore they instituted six, corresponding to the six weekdays, so that each family would have its day. And Ze’iri said: to a bull, a calf, a lamb, a ram, a kid and a goat. And why all this? Because they did not want to use the surplus of money for a bull for anything but a bull, and likewise for each one. And even though there is [one who says] in the first chapter of Shevuot (12b) that they use a bird burnt offering for the “dessert” of the altar, that is after the fact; but ab initio not, for it is better to use them for what they were originally designated.

notes.he: וששה לנדבה לצורך עולות הבאות מן המותרות שמותרות מדמי חטאת ואשם ושאר קרבנות משימין באותן שופרות וקונין מהן עולה:
notes.en: And six for gift offerings: for burnt offerings that come from the surplus; for the surplus from the money of a sin offering, a guilt offering and other offerings they put into those horns, and they buy burnt offerings with it.

messages.caption: The thirteen horns in the Temple, as the mishna lists them

messages.text: The funds contained in the six horns designated for communal gift offerings were used to purchase burnt offerings that come from the surplus funds which had been allocated for the purchase of sin offerings or guilt offerings and were not needed for those purposes. Such burnt offerings were brought in the absence of other offerings, so that the altar would not remain idle. Unlike other burnt offerings, the hides of these offerings were not given to the priests; rather, they were sold, and the money received from their sale was allocated for additional communal gift offerings. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
messages.lead: And it is taught with regard to that mishna:

notes.he: אלא חוזרין ומוכרין אותו ולוקחין בהמות לעולה לקיץ המזבח:
notes.en: That its hide does not go to the priests: rather, they sell it again and buy animals as burnt offerings for the “dessert” [kayitz] of the altar.

notes.he: [ואין עורה לכהנים דברי ר' יהודה אלא מוכרין אותן ולוקחין מדמיהן עולה:
notes.en: [And its hide does not go to the priests; the statement of Rabbi Yehuda: rather, they sell the hides and buy a burnt offering with their money.]

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda If so, the teaching of Jehoiada the High Priest has been negated.
messages.quote: the hides of these offerings were not given to the priests

notes.dh: א"ל ר' שמעון א"כ דאין עורן לכהנים] ביטל מדרשו של יהוידע הכהן דתניא
notes.he: אשם הוא משמע אשם נאכל לכהנים וכתי' אשם לה' כיצד יתקיימו ב' כתובים הללו:
notes.en: [Rabbi Shimon said to him: If so, that their hides do not go to the priests,] he has negated the midrash of Jehoiada the priest. As it is taught: “It is a guilt offering” implies a guilt offering eaten by the priests, and it is written “a guilt offering to the Lord” [Leviticus 5:19]. How can these two verses both be fulfilled? [Rabbeinu Gershom names only Rabbi Shimon, where the daf says Rabbi Neḥemya, and some say Rabbi Shimon.]

messages.text: This teaching was taught by Jehoiada the High Priest: There is an apparent contradiction in a verse. On the one hand, the verse states: “It is a guilt offering” (Leviticus 5:19), indicating that the meat of this guilt offering is eaten by the priests, as is the halakha with regard to all guilt offerings. On the other hand, the same verse concludes: “He is certainly guilty before the Lord,” which indicates that the entire offering is for God, like a burnt offering.
messages.lead: As it is taught in the aforementioned mishna:

verse.en: It is a reparation offering; they have incurred guilt before GOD.

messages.text: Rather, the verse comes to include the following halakha: With regard to anything that comes from surplus funds designated for sin offerings or guilt offerings, those funds should be used to purchase burnt offerings. The meat of these burnt offerings is entirely for God, and the hides are given to the priests, as is the halakha with regard to burnt offerings.

notes.he: חטאת וממותר אשם שילקח מהן עולות ויהא בשר לשם כליל ועורות לכהנים ויתקיימו שניהן אלמא אית ליה לר' שמעון נדבה ממותר חטאת ולא איצטריך למימר:
notes.en: To include that which comes from the surplus of a sin offering and from the surplus of a guilt offering: that burnt offerings be bought with it, and the meat be entirely for God and the hides for the priests, and both verses are fulfilled. Evidently Rabbi Shimon holds of gift offerings from the surplus of a sin offering, and [Rabbi Ami] did not need to say it.

messages.text: Apparently, Rabbi Shimon does hold that surplus funds which were designated for sin offerings are allocated for communal gift offerings. The statement of Rabbi Ami is therefore unnecessary even according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

It was necessary for Rabbi Ami to teach this halakha, as it might enter your mind to say: When Rabbi Shimon holds that surplus money which was designated for a sin offering is allocated for communal gift offerings, that applies only in a case where the surplus is from one set of money, e.g., one allocated funds to purchase a goat and the price of goats depreciated, and therefore there is now a surplus from the money that was set aside.

notes.he: וכגון הפריש שתי ציבורי מעות לחטאתו והוזלו הטלאים וניתותרו מן המעות:
notes.en: In one set: for example, where he designated two piles of money for his sin offering, and lambs became cheaper, and some of the money was left over. [So the printed Rashi; Rabbeinu Gershom here speaks of a single pile.]

notes.he: איצטריך סד"א כי אית ליה נדבה לרבי שמעון ממותר חטאת ה"מ בחד סידרא כגון שלא הפריש אלא צבור אחד מעות לשם חטאת וניתותרו מהן:
notes.en: It was necessary: it might enter your mind to say that when Rabbi Shimon holds of gift offerings from the surplus of a sin offering, that applies in one set, for example where he designated only one pile of money for a sin offering and some of it was left over.

messages.text: Continues on 24a: but where one designated two sets of money, as with a second set set aside as a guarantee, one might think that Rabbi Shimon does not allocate the surplus for gift offerings, so Rabbi Ami teaches that even then he does.
